quest.title: The Rhythm that Nurtures the Sprout
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #I will become a smart Aranara, just like Nara {NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Head to the designated location to look for clues about Ashvattha's Concourses

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We now have the second Vasoma Fruit!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Impressive! Nara {NICKNAME} is not afraid of Marana and even drove all the monsters away. No wonder you could defeat Vanagni!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, the many adventures we've been through aren't just for show, y'know?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #That's great! Then Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon must have many memories and stories, right?

choices.text: We do have a great many, yes.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #I see. If you don't mind, we'd love to hear Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon's stories sometime.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure! We've shared our stories with others before, though it feels like so long ago...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, Paimon saw a giant purple tree in the distance while we were in the Vasara Tree's dream. Paimon's pretty sure we saw it in Vanarana, too. What was that?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: That's the very first Ashvattha's Tree of Dreams. Hmm, how should I put this...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Dreams are like leaves in a stream. They soon float away with the water. If you want to keep a dream in place, you have to let it grow roots. That way, the dream won't drift away.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Hmm... it's so hard to explain...

choices.text: So Ashvattha's Tree of Dreams is like their "roots"?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} is smart. This tree keeps Aranara's dreams stable. Aranara can enter or exit dreams and are able to connect with the Vasara Tree.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's how it is. Do you mean, then, that the Vanarana in dreams can be maintained because of that tree?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: It is because of the Tree of Dreams. But I'm very concerned about Marana right now. We'll have to come up with a plan later.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #But let's get the Bija first! We need to help the friend of Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and Arana!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Will you be looking for other Ashvattha's Concourses after this, Arama?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes! So we'll see each other again for sure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stay safe, Arama!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #You too, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

choices.text: So Ashvattha's Tree of Dreams keeps dreams from drifting away?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arama! Here we are again!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Yes! Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Hello! This is Arasudraka.

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: #Ooh! Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Nice to meet you! The Golden Nara is tall and strong, just like the song says!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's really happy to meet you, too! Is Arasudraka a friend of yours, Arama?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Yes! Arasudraka is a "song gatherer" and often goes to collect all sorts of songs.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Before seeds became saplings, we hid in the leaves together and went to the Dendro Archon's big tree. We watched the Nara sing as they drank water that made them turn silly!

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, do you know any songs?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Songs... If it were that green fellow, he should know plenty of them!

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: The green fellow? What's that? A Dusk Bird? A Shroomboar?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no! He is the Anemo Archon of Mondstadt, and also a bard.

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: Wow! Then he must know a lot of songs!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Amazing! The Anemo Archon must be able to blow the songs to faraway places with the wind!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! Speaking of which, is this one of Ashvattha's Concourses?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: No, it is not. But it is a great discovery nonetheless. Here lies a song that we Aranara have been unable to find for many, many years.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Aranara song gatherers always pursue the beauty of songs. At the end of time, they will leave behind a song that belongs only to themselves.

choices.text: Does this have anything to do with Ashvattha's Concourses?

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: Seems like here is a song left by Aramaha. If it's true, there should be a Vasara Tree nearby!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon remembers Araja saying something about the Vasara Trees... Let Paimon check the Aranyaka real quick...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Vasara Trees bear Vasoma Fruits! We should help them, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yay! I get to study songs of the past with Nara!

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: Aramaha loves this type of rose, but it was Arayama who discovered the way to hide songs in roses! Arayama was proud, so Arayama's roses are proud, too.

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: So the roses won't tell us. Only a smart Aranara, or maybe a smart Nara, can find the hidden song. But Arasudraka is not smart enough...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Don't worry! Hehe, {NICKNAME} is very smart!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! And anyway, finding stuff is what we do best!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}! This seems to be the song left by Aramaha. If it's true, there should be a Vasara Tree nearby. We lucked out!

talks.objective: Observe the Sumeru Roses to find the hidden song

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: "Come, come, dreams of the sprouts, memories of the leaves..."

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: "Look, shining pomegranates, glowing Sunsettias..."

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: I see. Aranaga's song and Aramaha's song have the same source...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean, the same source...?

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: Songs are like rivers. They derive from the same origin, the "Sourcesong." She is the home to all songs and the source of all great rivers.

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: Then, it changes when it is sung for different memories and different stories, just like how a great river diverges into creeks.

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: Just like all the creeks eventually flow into the sea, all the songs eventually converge into one, into the Sourcesong.

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: #So Aranara song gatherers have to find all the songs. That way, we can find the Sourcesong. Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, for finding Aramaha's song.

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: #Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Songs will keep growing in numbers and changing along the way, so how can all the songs be found?

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: And so will Aranara. So, if we keep doing our best, there will be no problem!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Aramaha's song can attract Healthy Dendrograna. His Ashvattha's Concourse should be sealed in the same way.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} found his song, which means we can get to Ashvattha's Concourse right away!

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: #Yes! Good luck, Nara {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and Arama! I'm going to get ready for Festival Utsava!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Leave it to us! See you at Festival Utsava, Arasudraka!

response.speaker: Arasudraka
response.text: Bye!

choices.text: But songs will keep growing in numbers...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I still need a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: I'll wait for you.

talks.objective: Unlock the road ahead using the Rhythm of the Sprout
Keep going and reach Ashvattha's Concourse
Investigate the trees inside Ashvattha's Concourse

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this... the Vasara Tree? Doesn't seem as lively as Paimon imagined...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Yes, Aramaha resisted very hard, and kept Marana under control to the side. If not, the nearby forest would have become even more terrible.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: All the leaves would fall and rot on the ground. The mushrooms would all become angry Fungi, and the birds and beasts would also lie down and return to the ground, leaving only hard white things behind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds really scary...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Yes, but thanks to Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, Marana has become a lot less troubling!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: If it were just Arama alone, it wouldn't have worked at all. I am too young and don't have many memories, so I am not as powerful as other Aranara.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #But with memories of adventuring together with Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon, my powers will grow!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Friends go on adventures together! That's the spirit!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: First, we must enter his dream to destroy Marana's lingering influence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a second... When you say "his dream," you mean that of the Vasara Tree?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: That's right. If you are ready, reach out your hand and enter his dream...

talks.objective: Talk to Arama and enter the Vasara Tree's dream

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Reach your hand out to the Vasara Tree...)

talks.objective: Talk to Arama and enter the Vasara Tree's dream

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Yes. This is a Vasoma Fruit.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: It is the accumulation of the dreams and memories gathered by the Vasara Tree. It's a precious fruit that can help us restore our strength.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: A large amount of energy must be consumed for the Ashvattha Tree to produce a Bija. That is why we must offer Vasoma Fruits.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Keep the Vasoma Fruit safe, Nara {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. You know what? Let's teach Arama the meaning of "treasure"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now then! "Treasure" refers to something very precious. This Vasoma Fruit contains lots of dreams and memories, and it can restore an Aranara's power. That makes it pretty rare and amazing, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: For things like Vasoma Fruits that are rare and precious, we call them "treasure"!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Ah, so this is what treasure means... I got it! Thank you, Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Araja said that we'll need more than one Vasoma Fruit. That means we need to find other Ashvattha's Concourses, right?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #That's right. I'll do my best to find them! So long, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See you later, Arama!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you thanking Paimon for...? Anyway, Araja said that we'll need more than one Vasoma Fruit. That means we need to find other Ashvattha's Concourses, right?

talks.objective: Explore the dream of the Vasara Tree

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't expect Marana's corruption to be here too...

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} is amazing. You drove Marana away easily this time, too.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Aramaha resisted very hard to keep Marana to the side. Without his help, things would have been worse in the nearby forests.

dialogues.speaker: Arama

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do we need to enter the dream of the Vasara Tree this time too?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: Yes. We must erase all traces of Marana's influence.

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: That's right. If you are ready, reach out your hand and enter his dream...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Next up, our third Vasoma Fruit!

choices.text: Let's do this for the Bija...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: There's also Marana here, but Aramaha resisted very hard and kept Marana under control to the side. If not, the nearby forest would have become even more terrible.

response.speaker: Arama

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: If you are ready, reach out your hand and enter his dream...

dialogues.speaker: Arasudraka
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} is very smart! That's great!

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME}, if you are ready, reach out your hand and enter his dream...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We got the third Vasoma Fruit! According to Araja, three Vasoma Fruits should be enough, right?

dialogues.speaker: Arama
dialogues.text: #Yes, that will do. Thank you, Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, you were the one helping us throughout, Arama. So why are you thanking us?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Well... It's because you are helping Arana, and Arana is my friend. So, thank you.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #And Nara {NICKNAME} has helped Arayasa, Aradasa, and Arasudraka find the ancient songs. They're my friends too. Thank you for that, too.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Finally, I'm so happy that I got to go on adventures with Nara {NICKNAME} and Paimon. So, thanks for that as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon had a good time too! Thank you, Arama!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, there are many signs of activity around Ashvattha's Concourses... Is there some story behind that?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: That's a story from long, long ago. I wasn't even a seed then. It was a time when all Nara could see Aranara and not a single Aranara was afraid of Nara.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: #Back then, Nara and Aranara helped each other. They played and sang together, just like Nara {NICKNAME} and I.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Song gatherers like Arayasa originally learned their craft from Nara.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Ashvattha's Concourses used to be where Nara and Aranara played together. But that was a long time ago.

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: After the horrible, horrible catastrophe occurred, Vanarana was devastated, and the concourses were left desolate...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's what happened...

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Yes, and it's a very scary tale indeed. I'm lucky that they are not memories to me — only stories.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Don't worry! Things will get better. Right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: We've found Ashvattha's Concourses and obtained three Vasoma Fruits. Next, I've got to help prepare for Festival Utsava and call some of my friends back from the forest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Best of luck, Arama! Paimon's super looking forward to the festival!

response.speaker: Arama
response.text: Me too! I'll see you guys soon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bye, Arama!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #...Are you tired, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: You've been the one helping us...

dialogues.text: Hmmm... Where is the song?
